title: How to Pray — The Essentials
subtitle: The five daily prayers, step by step from standing to salaam
steps: Niyyah (intention) — settle the heart on which prayer and how many rak'ahs; the Prophet ﷺ said: actions are judged by intentions (Bukhari 1). Intention is in the heart, not spoken aloud.

Face the qiblah, standing. Say Allahu Akbar raising the hands (to the level of the shoulders, as reported in Bukhari 735; to the ears is also reported, Muslim 391) — the prayer has begun: its opening is the takbir and its closing is the taslim (Abu Dawud 61, hasan sahih per al-Albani).

Recite the opening supplication (thana') if you know it, then Surah al-Fatihah — the Prophet ﷺ said the prayer of one who does not recite it is not valid (Bukhari 756) — and then, in the first two rak'ahs, another surah or some verses of the Qur'an.
Ruku' — bow with the back level, saying Subhana Rabbiyal-'Azim three times.
Stand from ruku' saying Sami'allahu liman hamidah... Rabbana wa lakal-hamd.
Sujud — prostrate on seven limbs: forehead (with nose), two hands, two knees, two feet — saying Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la three times (Bukhari 812).
Sit between the two prostrations, then prostrate again — that is one rak'ah. Repeat per the prayer: Fajr 2, Dhuhr 4, Asr 4, Maghrib 3, Isha 4.
In the final sitting: the tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, and any dua; then the salaam: Assalamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah, turning right then left (Bukhari 831).
madhhabNote: Differences between the four schools (hand positions, recitation aloud vs silent, amin aloud) are all valid — the Huda rule: follow one school's fiqh completely, or ask a local teacher.

goDeeper.why: Prayer is a meeting, not a performance — each position carries a meaning: standing in awe, bowing in humility, prostration in nearness (Muslim 482: the nearest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make much supplication).
goDeeper.evidence: Each step above carries its own source in brackets; the full list is under Sources below.
goDeeper.commonMistakes: Rushing the words while the heart is elsewhere; looking around during prayer; treating wudu as a formality rather than the threshold of the meeting.

title: Wudu — The Purifying Wash
subtitle: How the Prophet ﷺ washed for prayer
steps: Niyyah in the heart, then Bismillah; the Prophet ﷺ said: there is no wudu for the one who does not mention Allah (Abu Dawud 101, sahih per al-Albani).
Wash the hands three times (Bukhari 159); the Prophet ﷺ liked to begin with the right side in purification (Bukhari 168).
Rinse the mouth and nose three times with one handful (Bukhari 159).
Wash the face three times — from the hairline to the chin, ear to ear.
Wash the arms to the elbows, right then left, three times (Qur'an 5:6).
Wipe the head once — wet hands from the forehead to the nape and back (Qur'an 5:6), then the ears.
Wash the feet to the ankles three times, right then left — the Prophet ﷺ said: woe to the heels from the Fire (Bukhari 163).
The seal: the shahada — Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah... and the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him (Muslim 234).

title: Ghusl — The Full Purification
subtitle: After janabah, menstruation's end, and before Friday prayer (sunnah)
steps: Niyyah in the heart; begin Bismillah.
Wash the hands, then wash the private parts — the Prophet ﷺ used to do this first (Bukhari 248).
Perform a complete wudu as for prayer (Bukhari 248).
Pour water over the head three times, letting it reach the roots of the hair — even under a thick braid (the matted-haired woman, Muslim 330).
Pour water over the head and then over the whole body, starting with the right side, so that no part is left dry (Bukhari 168, 248).

Friday ghusl: the Prophet ﷺ said it is a duty on every adult (Bukhari 879) and wished his companions to keep themselves clean on that day (Bukhari 902); scholars differ on whether it is obligatory or strongly recommended — ask a scholar.
madhhabNote: Order differs between schools (some wash the whole body first, wudu after) — all trace to the Prophet's ﷺ practice; follow your school's fiqh.

title: Tayammum — The Dry Purification
subtitle: When water is absent, harmful, or out of reach
steps: Condition: no water, or water would harm (illness, cold), or no access. The command: 'and if you are ill or on a journey... then seek clean earth' (Qur'an 4:43, 5:6).
Strike the clean earth (dust, sand, stone) once with both palms.
Wipe the face with them (Qur'an 4:43).
Strike the earth again — and wipe the hands and arms to the elbows (Qur'an 5:6).
Pray with it — the Prophet ﷺ said the earth has been made a place of prayer and a means of purification (Bukhari 335).

When water becomes available the need for tayammum ends: the Prophet ﷺ told a man in janabah who had no water to use clean earth, and later water was brought for him to pour over himself (Bukhari 344).

title: The Adhan & Iqamah
subtitle: The call that empties the unseen world of devils
steps: The mu'adhin faces the qiblah, raises the voice, and calls: Allahu Akbar (4x), Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah (2x), Ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah (2x), Hayya 'alas-salah (2x), Hayya 'alal-falah (2x), Allahu Akbar (2x), La ilaha illa Allah (Muslim 379).
In Fajr, after Hayya 'alal-falah: As-salatu khayrun minan-nawm (2x) (Abu Dawud 500, sahih per al-Albani).
The effect: Shaytan hears the adhan and flees, passing wind until he cannot hear it (Bukhari 608).
Repeat after the mu'adhin, and after the last phrase send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ — your intercession becomes obligatory for him (Muslim 384).
Then ask: Allahumma rabba hadhihid-da'watit-tammah... — the Prophet ﷺ said whoever says it, my intercession for him will be allowed on the Day of Resurrection (Bukhari 614).

The iqamah: the same words as adhan, doubled phrases said once, ending with Qad qamatis-salat (2x) — prayed immediately after it. (The iqamah wording is taught in the same chapters of the sunan; ask your imam for your local practice.)
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 614; Sahih Muslim 379, 384; Sunan Abi Dawud 500 (sahih per al-Albani; covers the adhan wording)

title: Friday Prayer — The Essentials
subtitle: Jumu'ah: the weekly gathering with conditions and sunnahs
steps: Obligatory on every Muslim except a slave, a woman, a boy and a sick person (Abu Dawud 1067, sahih per al-Albani).
Take the ghusl before it: the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever comes to the Friday prayer should bathe (Bukhari 877), and that it is a duty on every adult (Bukhari 879).
Wear the best clean clothes; early arrival is multiplied — the Prophet ﷺ compared the stages of arrival to sacrifices: as if a camel, then a cow, then a sheep... (Bukhari 881).
Listen in silence: even telling a companion 'be quiet' while the imam is giving the khutbah counts as idle talk (Bukhari 934).
The prayer: the Friday prayer is two rak'ahs, led by the imam after the khutbah.
The missed window: Jumu'ah has a fixed hour when no Muslim asks Allah but He grants it — the Prophet ﷺ indicated it is between the imam sitting and the prayer's end (Bukhari 935).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 877, 881, 934, 935; Sunan Abi Dawud 1067 (sahih per al-Albani)

title: Making Up Missed Prayers
subtitle: Qada' — the debt that only you can pay
steps: The duty: a missed obligatory prayer must be made up. The Prophet ﷺ taught that there is no omission in sleeping; omission is for the one who does not pray until the time of the next prayer comes (Muslim 681).
Pray it as soon as remembered — the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when he remembers it, and that there is no expiation for it other than that (Bukhari 597).
Order: keep the prayers in sequence when possible; if several prayers are owed and only part can be caught, begin with the earliest missed (the majority view).
Do not swap it for voluntary prayers: the only expiation for a missed prayer is to pray it when it is remembered (Muslim 684) — the missed prayer stands as a debt until it is prayed.

Practical system (a method, not a hadith): keep a simple count of what you owe and pray one or more qada prayers alongside each day's prayers until the count is cleared. The Gentle Ledger on My Journey can keep the count.
Ask: if sleep, travel, or genuine forgetfulness caused the miss — pray it without blame; deliberate neglect is the danger, and its cure is repentance plus immediate qada.
madhhabNote: The schools differ on whether multiple missed prayers must be prayed in strict order (hanafi: yes, with cause for exception; shafi'i: recommended; hanbali: obligatory). Follow your school.

title: The Rawatib — Prayers Around the Obligatory
subtitle: The sunnah prayers that guard the fard
steps: Fajr: two sunnah rak'ahs — 'the two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it' (Muslim 725).
Dhuhr: four before (and two after) — 'if anyone prays four before Dhuhr and four after, Allah forbids him the Fire' (Tirmidhi 428, sahih per Darussalam).
Maghrib: two after; Isha: two after.
The night prayer (qiyam): two by two — 'the night prayer is two by two, and witr is one rak'ah' (Bukhari 990).
Witr: the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned it, neither traveling nor resident (Bukhari 990).
Duha: the mid-morning prayer — 'a prayer of the repentant, prayed when the young camels feel the sun's heat' (Muslim 748).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 990; Sahih Muslim 725, 748; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 428 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Mosque Manners
subtitle: The adab of the house of Allah
steps: Enter with the right foot and the dua: Bismillah, was-salatu was-salamu 'ala Rasulillah... (reported in Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of the Mosques; number and grade not yet verified in this app).
Pray the two rak'ahs of greeting (tahiyyat al-masjid) before sitting — 'when one of you enters the mosque, let him not sit until he prays two rak'ahs' (Bukhari 444).
Keep the voice low: the Prophet ﷺ taught that worshippers should not disturb one another by reciting loudly in the mosque or in prayer (Abu Dawud 1332, sahih per al-Albani).
Do not pass in front of a praying person — the Prophet ﷺ said to prevent anyone who tries to pass between you and your sutra (Bukhari 509).
Leave with the left foot and the leaving-dua (inverse of the entering).
Eating, trade and loud talk are for elsewhere; even raw garlic or onion: the Prophet ﷺ said whoever eats them should keep away from the mosque (Bukhari 855).

title: Entering & Leaving the Home
subtitle: Bismillah at the door, gratitude at the threshold
steps: Enter with the right foot, saying Bismillah; the Prophet ﷺ named the entering-dua (Bismillah, was-salamu... ) — 'Shaytan then says to his companion: no lodging or supper for you tonight' (Muslim 2018).
Mention Allah over food and drink — 'mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest you' (Bukhari 5376).
Leave with the left foot and the leaving-dua: Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'alallah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

The greeting inside: spread the salam — 'you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another; shall I guide you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the salam among you' (Muslim 54).

title: Washing the Deceased
subtitle: Ghusl al-mayyit — the final service, done gently
steps: The washer should be trustworthy and keep the body covered; men wash men and women wash women, and a spouse may wash the other — this is the practice recorded in the fiqh books, not a hadith ruling; ask a scholar for the details of your school.
The Prophet ﷺ said of the washer: 'wash her three times, or five, or seven — odd numbers — and begin with her right side and the places of wudu' (Bukhari 1253, 1254).
Camphor is used in the final wash — apply camphor at the last wash (Bukhari 1253, Umm Atiyyah).
Wash gently and with care: the Prophet's daughter was washed with lotus-leaf water and shrouded in his garment (Abu Dawud 3142, sahih per al-Albani).
The water used last is poured with the du'a for forgiveness — 'O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, pardon him...' (Muslim 963; the Prophet ﷺ prayed this way over the deceased).

title: The Funeral Prayer
subtitle: Salat al-janazah — no ruku', no sujud, only dua
steps: Stand in rows facing the qiblah; the Prophet ﷺ stood at the middle of the body of a woman who had died (Bukhari 1331); where the imam stands for a man differs between the schools — ask a scholar.

Four takbirs: Allahu Akbar, then the opening supplication (al-Thanaiya); Allahu Akbar, then blessings on the Prophet ﷺ; Allahu Akbar, then the dua for the deceased (four takbirs: Muslim 951; the dua: Muslim 963).
The dua: Allahumma-ghfir lahu, warhamhu, wa 'afihi, wa'fu 'anhu... — the Prophet ﷺ taught it, and for a woman, the endings change (Muslim 963).
A fourth takbir, then one may add a personal dua; the salam follows — one salam to the right (most schools).

The reward: 'whoever follows a funeral and prays over it, he earns a qirat; and whoever stays until the burial, two qirats' — the companions asked: what are two qirats? He said: like two great mountains (Bukhari 1325).

title: The Burial & Visiting Graves
subtitle: Hasten the burial; visit to remember, not to worship
steps: Hasten it: 'hasten with the deceased, for if it was righteous, you are forwarding it to good; and if otherwise, you are taking a burden off your necks' (Bukhari 1315).
The grave: dug as a lahd (niche) where the ground allows; the body laid on its right side facing the qiblah.

The earth is thrown — three handfuls from the head's end (Ibn Majah 1565, hasan per Darussalam). Many scholars add the words 'minha khalaqnakum...' (from Qur'an 20:55); that addition is reported in a weaker narration.

No wailing, no fire-brands of grief, no bare heads from grief itself — the Prophet ﷺ said 'the deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over him' (Muslim 927; scholars discuss exactly what this means, and Aisha (RA) explained it in Bukhari 1286-1288).
Visiting graves: the Prophet ﷺ permitted it — 'I had forbidden you to visit graves, but now visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter' (Muslim 977).
The greeting of the grave: Assalamu 'alaykum ahlal-qubur... (Muslim 977).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1286, 1315; Sahih Muslim 927, 977; Sunan Ibn Majah 1565 (hasan per Darussalam)

title: Consoling the Bereaved
subtitle: What to say when there is nothing to say
steps: The sunnah phrase: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; Allahumma-jurni fi musibati, wakhluf li khayran minha — 'O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with better' (Muslim 918).

Say what eases: the Prophet ﷺ said: 'whoever consoles a person with an affliction has the same reward as him' (Tirmidhi 1073 — daʿif per Darussalam, so take it as encouragement, not a firm promise; the wording says any affliction).
Do not say 'it could be worse' or 'be strong' — the sunnah is to speak the phrases of tawhid and reward.
Serve the family: bring food — 'the family of Ja'far are preoccupied; feed them' (Abu Dawud 3132, hasan per al-Albani).
Mourning is limited: the Prophet ﷺ allowed three days of mourning for the dead, and four months and ten days for a widow (Bukhari 1280).
Pray for the dead in their absence: a righteous child's prayer keeps reaching the dead (Muslim 1631).
sources: Sahih Muslim 918; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1073 (daʿif per Darussalam)

title: Eating Manners
subtitle: One-third for food, one-third for drink, one-third for breath
steps: Say Bismillah; if forgotten: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu (Abu Dawud 3767, sahih per al-Albani).
Eat with the right hand — 'the Shaytan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left' (Muslim 2020).
Eat from what is nearest — 'eat from what is nearest to you' (Bukhari 5376).

The portion: 'the son of Adam fills no vessel worse than his stomach — a few morsels suffice him; but if he must, then one-third for food, one-third for drink, one-third for breath' (Ibn Majah 3349, sahih per Darussalam).
Eat together — 'the food of one suffices two, and the food of two suffices four' (Bukhari 5392).
Praise after: Alhamdulillahil-ladhi at'amana... — 'Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel and praises Him for it' (Muslim 2734).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5376, 5392; Sahih Muslim 2020, 2734; Sunan Ibn Majah 3349 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Sleeping Manners
subtitle: The night as worship's gateway
steps: Before bed: ayat al-Kursi — 'a guardian from Allah stays with you and no devil approaches you until morning' (Bukhari 2311).
The three quls: blow into the palms, wipe over what you can reach of the body (Bukhari 5017).
Sleep on the right side — 'when you go to bed, lie on your right side' (Bukhari 247).
The duas: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya; and on waking: Alhamdulillahil-ladhi ahyana... (Bukhari 6324).

A surah that intercedes: al-Mulk — 'there is a surah of thirty verses which intercedes for a man until he is forgiven: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion' (Abu Dawud 1400, hasan per al-Albani). The Prophet ﷺ also used to recite it with as-Sajdah before sleeping (Tirmidhi 3404, hasan per Darussalam).
The night is also for prayer: 'the best prayer after the obligatory is the night prayer' (Muslim 1163).

title: Speech — The Weight of Words
subtitle: Guarding the tongue without going silent
steps: The standard: 'whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent' (Bukhari 6018).
The backbite prohibition: 'would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You detest it!' (49:12).

The limit of the prohibition: backbiting and prying into hidden faults are forbidden (Abu Dawud 4880, hasan sahih per al-Albani). Scholars allow naming a wrong when it is needed to stop it or to seek justice (see Qur'an 4:148) — ask a scholar for the limits.
Argue gently: 'I guarantee a house at the edge of Paradise for the one who leaves an argument even when he is right' (Abu Dawud 4800, hasan per al-Albani).
Praise with honesty: 'the one who deceives us is not one of us' (Muslim 101).
The dua: Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik — 'O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You well' (Abu Dawud 1522, sahih per al-Albani).
sources: Qur'an 49:12; Sahih al-Bukhari 6018; Sahih Muslim 101; Sunan Abi Dawud 4800, 4880 (hasan per al-Albani)

title: Greetings & Sneezing
subtitle: The salam as a transaction of peace
steps: Spread the salam: 'as-salamu 'alaykum' — to those you know and those you do not (Bukhari 12).
The return: wa 'alaykum as-salam — and the reward: 'you will not enter Paradise until you love one another; spread the salam among you' (Muslim 54).
Sneezing: the sneezer says Alhamdulillah; the hearer says Yarhamukallah; the sneezer returns: Yahdikumullah... (Bukhari 6224).
Yawning is from Shaytan — suppress it: 'yawning is from Shaytan, so if any of you yawns let him suppress it as much as he can' (Bukhari 6226).
The handshake completes the greeting: 'when two Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall away before they part' (Abu Dawud 5212, sahih per al-Albani).
Enter gatherings with the salam; leave with it — the salam begins and ends every sitting.

title: Hajj — The Fifth Pillar
subtitle: Who must go, when, and what it requires
steps: The obligation: 'And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to undertake it' (3:97) — ability means provision, health, route safety, and the family's maintenance during absence.
The condition of islam: Hajj of a non-Muslim is not accepted; the Qur'an likens the deeds of those who disbelieve to a mirage (24:39).
Once in a lifetime — the Prophet ﷺ was asked if the newly performed Hajj was for every year: 'no; the Hajj is once; what exceeds that is voluntary' (Muslim 1337).
The timing: Hajj is in specific days of Dhul-Hijjah (2:197) — the 8th to the 13th; Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Before departure: settle debts, write a will, seek forgiveness, leave the family's provision — Umar kept the emigrants' deposits in trust; a pilgrim's household is a trust too.

The reward: 'from one Umrah to another is expiation for what is between them, and the accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise' (Bukhari 1773); and whoever performs Hajj without obscenity or sin returns as on the day his mother bore him (Bukhari 1521).

title: Ihram — Entering the Sacred State
subtitle: Two cloths, two rak'ahs, one talbiyah
steps: Perfume the body before the niyyah, not after — Aisha perfumed the Prophet ﷺ when he entered ihram (Bukhari 1539). A ghusl before ihram is also commonly recommended; ask a scholar of your school.

Men: two seamless white cloths; no fitted garments, no head covering — 'the muhrim wears no turban, no hooded cloak, no trousers...' (Bukhari 134). Women wear ordinary modest dress; no face veil, no gloves (Bukhari 1838).

Pray at the miqat (at Wadi al-Aqiq the Prophet ﷺ was told: 'pray in this blessed valley', Bukhari 1534), then state the niyyah: Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan (or 'Umratan) — and the umrah niyyah suffices until the Hajj days.
The talbiyah, raised aloud by men: Labbaika Allahu labbaik, labbaika la sharika laka labbaik... — the Prophet ﷺ said: Jibril instructed me to keep raising it (Muslim 1184).

What ihram forbids: sewn garments (men), head covering (men), face cover and gloves (women), cutting hair or nails, perfume, hunting, marriage contracts — 'the muhrim may not marry, nor be married' (Muslim 1409).
Violations are expiated by fidyah — fasting three days, feeding six poor people, or sacrificing a sheep (2:196); the schools detail which applies to which violation.
madhhabNote: Which violations require which expiation differs by school and cause (perfume vs shaving vs intimacy) — this is exactly the case for a Hajj seminar or a trusted fiqh manual, not a quick card.

title: Tawaf & Sa'i
subtitle: Seven circuits and seven lengths — the rites Hajar taught us
steps: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram with the right foot and the dua; approach the Black Stone — kiss it if you can (Umar kissed it, saying he did so only because he had seen the Prophet ﷺ do it: Bukhari 1597), or point to it from where you stand, as the Prophet ﷺ pointed to the corner from his mount (Bukhari 1612).

Tawaf: seven circuits beginning and ending at the Stone, the Kaaba on your LEFT — counterclockwise; the first three rounds are ramal (brisk, chest out) for men in the arrival tawaf (ramal: Bukhari 1602).

Between circuits, at the Yemeni corner and the Stone: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah... (reported in Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of the Rites of Hajj; number and grade not yet verified in this app); two rak'ahs of tawaf behind the Maqam after completion (2:125).
Then sa'i: between Safa and Marwah seven lengths (Safa→Marwah = one), remembering Hajar's search — 'then she descended... and hurried as a person hurries in distress' (Bukhari 3364).
Men jog between the two green markers, the stretch where Hajar hurried; the Prophet's own sa'i is described in Jabir's account of his Hajj (Muslim 1218).

Completion of Umrah: the men shave (the Prophet ﷺ prayed for those who shave and then for those who shorten, Bukhari 1727) or shorten; women do not shave; clipping is what is required of them (Abu Dawud 1984, sahih li ghayrihi per al-Albani).

title: The Day of Arafah
subtitle: The day the religion was perfected
steps: Stand at Arafat — the Prophet ﷺ said: the Hajj is Arafat; and whoever reaches Jam' (Muzdalifah) at night before Fajr has caught the Hajj (Tirmidhi 889, sahih per Darussalam).
The timing: presence within the boundaries from noon until sunset; departure after sunset is sunnah (most scholars).

The dua of the day: the Prophet ﷺ said the best dua is the dua of Arafah — La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (Tirmidhi 3585 — daʿif per Darussalam; al-Tirmidhi called it hasan gharib, so take it as encouragement).
The forgiveness: 'there is no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire than the day of Arafah' (Muslim 1348).
For the non-pilgrim: fasting Arafah expiates the year before and the year after — for those not on Hajj (Muslim 1162).
The perfection: on this day, at Arafat, the verse descended: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you' (5:3).
sources: Qur'an 5:3; Sahih Muslim 1162, 1348; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 889 (sahih per Darussalam), 3585 (daʿif per Darussalam)

title: Fasting — The Fourth Pillar
subtitle: From dawn to sunset, and what breaks the fast
steps: The obligation: 'O believers, fasting is prescribed for you as it was for those before you' (2:183) — Ramadan by sighting the moon: 'fast when you see it and break when you see it' (Bukhari 1909).
The niyyah is settled each night before dawn — the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever does not resolve to fast before dawn has no fast (Abu Dawud 2454, sahih per al-Albani).
What breaks it: eating, drinking, and marital relations (2:187); the Prophet ﷺ listed the one who eats forgetting and continues — 'it is Allah who fed him and gave him drink' (Bukhari 1933).
What does not: tasting food without swallowing (with need), the siwak, rinsing the mouth, nose drops (the majority), eye drops — scholars differ on some of these; ask a scholar for your case.
The exemptions with make-up: illness and travel — 'whoever is ill or on a journey, a number of other days' (2:184); the pregnant and nursing feed a poor person per day (fidyah) per the majority.
The night is for eating: 'take the pre-dawn meal, for in the suhoor there is blessing' (Bukhari 1923).
madhhabNote: The details of make-up vs fidyah for the elderly, pregnancy, and chronic illness differ by school — consult a local mufti for your case.

title: Ramadan Nights
subtitle: Taraweeh, the khatm, and Laylat al-Qadr
steps: The prayer: the Prophet ﷺ led the companions in congregation for a few nights, then discontinued, saying: 'I feared it would be made obligatory for you' (Bukhari 1129).

Umar established the congregational taraweeh with twenty rak'ahs — 'what an excellent innovation this is' (Bukhari 2010 narration context); eight or twenty are both practiced among the pious predecessors.
The pace: Jibril met the Prophet ﷺ every night of Ramadan and they reviewed the Qur'an together (Bukhari 6); aim for recitation you can sustain thirty nights.

Laylat al-Qadr: better than a thousand months (97:3) — in the odd nights of the last ten; Aisha asked what to say if she found it: Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni (Tirmidhi 3513, sahih per Darussalam).
The i'tikaf: seclusion in the mosque for the last ten days — the Prophet ﷺ did i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan until Allah took him (Bukhari 2026).
The generosity: the Prophet ﷺ was more generous in Ramadan than the free wind (Bukhari 6).
sources: Qur'an 97; Sahih al-Bukhari 6, 1129, 2024; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3513, sahih per Darussalam
madhhabNote: Taraweeh length (8 vs 20 rak'ahs) is a difference of practice among the schools and the salaf — both are sound; follow your local congregation without argument.

title: Istikhara — The Guidance Prayer
subtitle: Two rak'ahs and the dua of surrender
steps: The need: 'when one of you intends a matter, let him pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory, then say...' — the full istikhara dua taught by the Prophet ﷺ (Bukhari 6382).

The dua's heart: 'O Allah, I ask Your guidance by Your knowledge, and power by Your might... If this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and my outcome, decree it for me and ease it; and if it is evil, turn it away from me and turn me from it, and decree good for me wherever it is' (Bukhari 6382).
Then act: istikhara is not a demand for a vision; the scholars said: 'seek the means, then act on what settles in the heart after the dua.'

The answer's forms: ease and opening (a sign to proceed), difficulty and closed doors (a sign to withdraw), or continued neutrality — in which case repeat up to seven days, then choose (per many scholars).
What it is not: a substitute for due diligence, consultation, or fiqh — 'the one who consults does not regret' (Tabarani, hasan).
What it is: the admission that outcomes belong to Allah — the worshipper asks to be steered, then walks with tawakkul.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6382; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 480 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Tawba — The Return
subtitle: Four conditions the scholars agreed upon
steps: The conditions: (1) abandon the sin now; (2) regret it sincerely; (3) resolve not to return; (4) restore the right if it was a violation of another's right — their property, their honor, or their due.
The door's hours: 'Allah accepts the servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat' (Tirmidhi 3537, hasan per Darussalam) — and the Prophet ﷺ added: until the sun rises from the west.
The replacement promise: 'except those who repent, believe, and do righteousness — Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones' (25:68-70).

For the habitual sinner: 'the one who repents from sin is as if he had no sin' (Ibn Majah 4250, weak per Darussalam); repeat the return without despair — the previous card in this library is Shaytan's despair-play.
The concealment: 'conceal the sin of your brother and Allah will conceal yours' — do not publicize past sins even in confession beyond need (Baihaqi).
The seal: the Prophet ﷺ taught: 'by the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would replace you with people who sin and seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them' (Muslim 2749).
sources: Qur'an 25:68-70; Sahih Muslim 2749; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3537, hasan per Darussalam

title: Earning — Halal Livelihood
subtitle: The body built from the unlawful will not enter Paradise
steps: The principle: 'Allah is pure and accepts only what is pure' (Muslim 1015) — 'the truthful merchant will be with the prophets, the truthful, and the martyrs' (Tirmidhi 1209 — daʿif per Darussalam, so take it as encouragement).
The prohibition core: 'Allah has cursed the one who consumes interest and the one who pays it' (Muslim 1598) — the contract is the sin, not only the receipt.
The scales: full measure — 'woe to the fraudsters... who take full measure when they receive but diminish when they give' (83:1-3); give the customer his due even when he does not check.
The honest broker: 'the two parties of a transaction have the option as long as they have not parted; if they were truthful and clear, their transaction is blessed' (Bukhari 2079).
The laborer: 'give the worker his wages before his sweat dries' (Ibn Majah 2443, sahih per Darussalam).
The doubtful: 'leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not' (Tirmidhi 2518, sahih per Darussalam).
sources: Qur'an 83:1-3; Sahih al-Bukhari 2079; Sahih Muslim 1015, 1598; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 1209 (daʿif per Darussalam), 2518 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Marriage — The Nikah
subtitle: Half the religion, in a contract of mercy
steps: The command frame: 'marry the spouseless among you' (24:32); 'when the servant marries, he has completed half of his religion' (Baihaqi, hasan).
The core condition: consent — the virgin is not married without her permission, and her silence is her permission (Bukhari 6946).
The sermon: the Prophet ﷺ addressed marriages with praise of Allah and the dua for barakah — 'and the best of you is the best of you to their wives' (Tirmidhi 3895, sahih per Darussalam).
The guardian: 'there is no marriage without the permission of a guardian' (Abu Dawud 2085, sahih per al-Albani); scholars also require two upright witnesses to the contract.
The mahr: a right owed to the bride, never a purchase (Qur'an 4:4); ask a scholar or your family elders what is customary and fair.
The spirit: 'the believers are but brothers' (49:10) begins at home — the Prophet ﷺ said the best of you is the best to his family, and he was the best to his (Tirmidhi 3895, sahih per Darussalam).
sources: Qur'an 24:32; 49:10; Sahih al-Bukhari 6946; Sunan Abi Dawud 2085 (sahih per al-Albani); Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3895 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Illness & Patience
subtitle: The fever as expiation, the visit as worship
steps: The expiation: 'no fatigue, nor illness, nor anxiety, nor sorrow, nor harm befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates by it — even the thorn' (Bukhari 5641).
The dua: 'O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm and heal; You are the Healer' — said over the sick seven times (Bukhari 5675).
The patience ranks: 'amazing is the affair of the believer... if harm reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999).
Visiting the sick: 'a Muslim has five rights over his brother: returning the salam, visiting the sick, attending the funeral, accepting invitations, and blessing the sneezer' (Muslim 2162).
The reminder: illness is a visitor with a purpose — the Prophet ﷺ would visit the sick and ask Allah to remove the harm and grant a complete cure (Bukhari 5675).
The worst moment: Allah has made a remedy for every illness He created, so seek treatment (Bukhari 5678).

title: Gratitude — Shukr
subtitle: The wealth that increases
steps: The root: 'if you are grateful, I will surely increase you' (14:7) — gratitude as the economics of the soul.
The tongue: say Alhamdulillah at every event, Alhamdulillah after every meal, Alhamdulillah 'alaa kulli hal — in ease and hardship (the Prophet's ﷺ practice in all states).
The heart: recognize the gift as a gift — the scholars called shukr 'the heart's acknowledgment of the blessing's source.'
The limbs: 'show gratitude to Allah' means worship — the prayer at the moment of blessing, the charity at the moment of increase.
The hardship form: the patient receive their reward without measure (Qur'an 39:10); gratitude and patience are twin tasks.
The completion: gratitude is the key to retention — blessings flee the ungrateful the way water flees a cracked vessel (Abu Dawud, hasan).
sources: Qur'an 14:7, 39:10; Sunan Abi Dawud 4811 (sahih per al-Albani)

title: Travel — The Wayfarer's Adab
subtitle: Provision, safety, and the dua of the road
steps: The intention: the Qur'an speaks of the road as a place of safety — 'Travel between them by night or day in safety' (34:18); set out with remembrance and a halal purpose.
The companionship: travel with the God-fearing and keep company that reminds you of Allah.
The boarding dua: Bismillah, Allahu Akbar (3x) — the Prophet ﷺ said: then Allah says: you are protected (Abu Dawud 2602, sahih per al-Albani).
The tawakkul form: 'Allahumma hawwin 'alayna safarana...' — the travel dua of the Prophet ﷺ (Muslim 1342).

The shortened prayer (qasr): four-rak'ah prayers are prayed two — 'there is no blame upon you in shortening the prayer if you fear' (4:101); most scholars add: while traveling beyond the city's edge, under conditions.
The return: repeat the boarding dua and add: ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, lirabbina hamidun — returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord (Muslim 1342).
sources: Qur'an 34:18; 4:101; Sahih Muslim 1342-1343; Sunan Abi Dawud 2602 (sahih per al-Albani)
madhhabNote: Qasr's distance and duration limits differ by school (the majority: ~85km and under ~15 days) — follow your school's fiqh for your journey.

title: The Morning & Evening Adhkar
subtitle: The fortress that takes seven minutes
steps: The time: morning — after Fajr until sunrise; evening — after Asr until Maghrib (per most scholars).
Ayat al-Kursi (once each) — 'whoever recites it in the morning and evening is protected until he recites it again' (Nasa'i).
The three quls: al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, an-Nas — three times each, blown into the hands and wiped over the body (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani).
The master dua: 'We have entered the morning (evening), and the kingdom belongs to Allah; the praise belongs to Allah...' (Muslim 2723).
Sayyid al-istighfar — the best form of seeking forgiveness, morning and evening (Bukhari 6306).
Protection scope: 'these suffice you against everything' — the Prophet ﷺ said of the mu'awwidhat for every harm (Abu Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6306; Sahih Muslim 2723; Sunan Abi Dawud 5082, hasan per al-Albani

title: The New Baby — Welcome Rites
subtitle: Adhan in the ear, tahnik, and the aqiqah
steps: The adhan: the Prophet ﷺ said the adhan in the ear of al-Hasan when he was born (Abu Dawud 5105, hasan per al-Albani) — the first sound a Muslim child hears.

The name: choose a good name — 'you will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and your fathers' names' (Abu Dawud 4948 — daʿif per al-Albani, so take it as encouragement); the Prophet ﷺ named on the seventh day (Abu Dawud 2838, sahih per al-Albani).
The tahnik: chew a date and rub the child's palate with it — the Prophet ﷺ did this for Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr when he was born and prayed for him (Bukhari 5469).
The aqiqah: two sheep for a boy, one for a girl — 'for the boy two equivalent sheep, and for the girl one' (Tirmidhi 1513, hasan per Darussalam); on the seventh day.
The shaving: the child's head is shaved on the seventh day (Abu Dawud 2838, sahih per al-Albani).
Pray for the child and congratulate the parents in your own words; no fixed formula is cited here.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 5467, 5472; Sunan Abi Dawud 5105 (hasan per al-Albani), 2838, 4948 (daʿif per al-Albani); Sunan at-Tirmidhi 1513 (hasan per Darussalam)

title: The Rights of Parents
subtitle: Paradise's gate is at their feet
steps: The command's weight: 'your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and goodness to parents' — joined to tawhid itself (17:23).
The smallest word: never say so much as 'uff' to them (17:23); the Prophet ﷺ listed disobedience to mothers among the forbidden things (Bukhari 5975).
The lowered wing: 'lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small' (17:24).
The order of service: the mother first, thrice over — 'who is most deserving of my good companionship? Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father' (Bukhari 5971).
After their passing: pray for them, give charity on their behalf, honor their friends — 'the finest of your fathers are the best of them' (Muslim 2552).
The duty's limit: obedience in goodness only — 'no obedience to any created being in disobedience to the Creator' (reported; number not verified).

title: The Rights of Neighbors
subtitle: Forty neighbors — and the one who does not harm them
steps: The measure: 'by Allah, he does not believe; by Allah, he does not believe' — the companions asked: who, O Messenger of Allah? He said: the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm (Bukhari 6016).
The scope: the neighbor's right is wide — whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day does not harm his neighbor (Bukhari 6018).
The Quran's own neighbors: 'worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor and the far neighbor' (4:36).
The practical form: share food, visit in illness, attend their funerals, shelter their good name — 'whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor' (Bukhari 6018).
The harm list: no smoke, no noise, no litter, no prying eyes over the fence — the Prophet ﷺ said: 'he does not enter Paradise whose neighbor is not safe from his harm.'
The test: the Prophet ﷺ was asked about a neighbor who harms: 'keep enduring his harm and seek Allah's help' — until, the scholars add, harm becomes unbearable, then seek counsel.

title: Oaths & Vows
subtitle: Swearing is a mortgage on the tongue
steps: The default: do not swear by other than Allah — 'whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk' (Tirmidhi 1535, sahih per Darussalam).
The caution: 'do not swear a lot in your buying and selling; it removes the blessing' (Bukhari 2087).
The inadvertent oath: feeding or clothing ten poor people, freeing a slave, or fasting three days — 'so its expiation is the feeding of ten poor people' (5:89).
The deliberate broken oath: same kaffarah — and Allah said: 'so protect your oaths' (5:89).

The vow (nadhr): the Prophet ﷺ said: 'it does not bring the son of Adam anything I decreed for him or turn away anything I decreed against; it only extracts from the miser' (Bukhari 6608) — yet once made, it must be kept.
The mercy: 'the expiation for a vow is its kaffarah' — and the scholars teach: if the vow's object becomes impossible or sinful, the vow dissolves by intention's failure, per school details.
sources: Qur'an 5:89; Sahih al-Bukhari 2087, 6608; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 1535 (sahih per Darussalam)

title: Witr & The Night Routine
subtitle: Closing the day the way it opened — with light
steps: The standing practice: the Prophet ﷺ never abandoned the witr, neither traveling nor resident — 'make the witr your last prayer at night' (Bukhari 990).
The qunut — the schools differ on its place: Hanafi: before ruku' in witr nightly; Shafi'i: in the second half of Ramadan; Hanbali: may be before or after; the evidence supports all.
The dua al-qunut wording the Prophet ﷺ taught (for the one who wishes to memorize): Allahumma-hdini fiman hadayt... (Nasai 1745, sahih per Darussalam).
The sleep-with-worship balance: if you fear missing Fajr, pray witr and sleep; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'there are no two witr in one night' (Abu Dawud 1439, sahih per al-Albani).
The ending: the last words before sleep — Subhan Allah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wallahu akbar (Bukhari 6306).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 990, 6306; Sunan an-Nasa'i 1745; Sunan Abi Dawud 1439 (sahih per al-Albani)
madhhabNote: Witr's timing (before or after sleep) and qunut's placement differ by school — all from the Prophet's ﷺ practice on different nights; follow one school consistently.

title: Seeking Knowledge
subtitle: The path walked slowly, with humility
steps: The intention: the Prophet ﷺ said: 'whoever seeks knowledge to compete, or to be praised, or to draw attention — his destination is the Fire' (Tirmidhi 2654 — daʿif per Darussalam, so take it as a warning to check your intention, not a verdict).
The humility equipment: 'whoever travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise' (Muslim 2699).
The manners before the teacher: sit where you are placed, do not argue, do not say 'but so-and-so said' — the salaf called the student's humility half the knowledge.
The pace: 'knowledge is by learning' — and the tradition adds: take from the mouths of the trustworthy, verify, and write.
The application test: 'knowledge is a shield; acting without knowledge is deviation' (Daraqutni) — the first knowledge to act on: prayer and its times.
The chain's honor: 'the scholars are the inheritors of the prophets' (Abu Dawud 3641, sahih per al-Albani).
sources: Sahih Muslim 2699; Sunan Abi Dawud 3641 (sahih per al-Albani); Sunan at-Tirmidhi 2654 (daʿif per Darussalam)

title: Hardship & Relief
subtitle: The dua of distress — the treasury of the tested
steps: The distress dua: 'La ilaha illa Allah, al-'azim, al-halim. La ilaha illa Allah, Rabbul-'arshil-'azim...' — the Prophet ﷺ said: no servant supplicates with it concerning anything except that Allah answers him (Bukhari 6346).
The anxious heart: 'Allahumma inni a'udhu bika minal-hammi wal-hazan...' — the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge in Allah from worry, grief, weakness, laziness, cowardice and debt (Bukhari 6369).

The debt: 'Allahumma akfini bihalalika 'an haramika...' — 'O Allah, suffice me with Your halal against Your haram, and enrich me by Your bounty from all besides You' (Tirmidhi 3563, hasan per Darussalam).
The grief response: recite the same dua of distress again and again (Bukhari 6346) — it is a treasury, not a one-time use.
The patience anchor: 'amazing is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him' (Muslim 2999).
The exit guarantee: 'whoever leaves a thing for Allah, Allah will give him something better' (Ahmad).
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6346, 6369; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3563 (hasan per Darussalam)

title: Preparing — The Practical Will
subtitle: Five duties every believer owes the future
steps: Write the will: 'it is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, to make a bequest...' (2:180) — the Prophet ﷺ said: a Muslim who has something to bequeath should not pass two nights without his will written (Bukhari 2738).
The debt ledger: record every debt, every trust, every unresolved claim — the martyr's sins are forgiven but his debts are settled first (Muslim 1886).

Teach your heirs the dua of the dying — 'whoever's last words are la ilaha illa Allah enters Paradise' (Abu Dawud 3116, sahih per al-Albani): practice saying it now, slowly, until it is the easiest sentence you own.
The funeral instructions: leave word for a simple janazah, no wailing, swift burial — 'hasten with the deceased' (Bukhari 1315).

The continuing charity: establish one sadaqah jariyah before death — a well, a tree, a student's tuition — the three things that keep paying: ongoing charity, useful knowledge, a righteous child (Muslim 1631).

The gentle end: keep the family reconciled — the Prophet ﷺ said: 'the doors of the Garden are opened on Mondays and Thursdays, and every servant who does not associate anything with Allah is forgiven except the man who has enmity between him and his brother' (Muslim 2565).

title: Hajj — The Fifth Pillar (Walkthrough)
subtitle: The full journey, day by day, from ihram to the farewell tawaf
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat (or before it for air travelers): ghusl, the two white cloths, the niyyah and talbiyah — Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan.
Day 1 (8 Dhul-Hijjah, Yawm at-Tarwiyah): enter ihram for Hajj if not already; proceed to Mina and pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr there, shortened but not combined.
Day 2 (9 Dhul-Hijjah, Arafah): stand at Arafat from noon until sunset — the essence of Hajj. Combine Dhuhr and Asr at Zuhr time, shortened. Pray, make dua, remember; no fasting for the pilgrim.
After sunset, leave for Muzdalifah without praying Maghrib at Arafat: pray Maghrib and Isha combined at Isha time; spend the night (or part of it, especially for the weak and women).

Day 3 (10 Dhul-Hijjah, Yawm an-Nahr): stone Jamrat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles; sacrifice; shave or shorten the hair (taqsir/halq) — the first release from ihram; then the tawaf al-ifadah and sa'i of Hajj, completing the release.
The days of Tashreeq (11-13): stone the three jamarat daily after noon, seven each — or leave after two days, the concession for those who hasten (2:203).
Farewell: before departing Makkah, the tawaf al-wada' — one final circuit. The menstruating woman is excused from it (Bukhari 1755).
madhhabNote: Stoning order details, Muzdalifah stay length, and combining prayers differ in detail between schools — follow your group's mutawwif (guide) or your school's fiqh.

title: Umrah — In a Day
subtitle: The smaller pilgrimage, complete from ihram to release
steps: Enter ihram at the miqat: ghusl, the cloths, niyyah for Umrah, talbiyah — Labbaika Allahumma Umrah.

Arrive al-Masjid al-Haram with the talbiyah still on your tongue; begin tawaf at the Black Stone (kiss, touch, or point with takbir), seven circuits, the Kaaba on your left, ramal (brisk) in the first three if others are present.
Pray two rak'ahs of tawaf behind the Maqam Ibrahim if possible; drink Zamzam.
Sa'i: Safa to Marwah seven lengths, remembering Hajar's run; men jog between the green lights.
Exit ihram: shave (preferred) or shorten the hair — the Umrah is complete. Men shorten from all sides; women cut a fingertip's length only.
No raml in sa'i after the first tawaf; no visit to the rawdah is required but is beloved if time allows.
madhhabNote: Women do not ramal and do not shave; touching the Black Stone is sunnah, never an obligation — the crowd's safety comes first.

title: The Day of Arafah — Even at Home
subtitle: The 9th of Dhul-Hijjah for the pilgrim and the one far away
steps: For the pilgrim: stand within the boundary of Arafat from noon to sunset — standing even a moment within it completes the pillar; combine Dhuhr and Asr at Zuhr time, two by two.
Fill the hours with dua — the best is the taught one: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir (Tirmidhi 3585, weak per Darussalam).
Do not fast on Arafah if you are the pilgrim standing there — the Prophet ﷺ was seen drinking milk at Arafah while the people watched (Bukhari 1661).
For everyone else: FAST this day — it expiates the year before and the year after (Muslim 1162); say the takbir and the shahada abundantly.
After sunset, depart for Muzdalifah — but not before the sun sets; the impatient crowds cannot move the sun.

The one who misses the standing at Arafah entirely has missed that Hajj ('Hajj is Arafah'); what he then owes is a ruling of the schools — ask a scholar. So the boundary signs matter; follow the guides.
sources: Sahih Muslim 1162, 1348; Sunan at-Tirmidhi 3585, weak per Darussalam
madhhabNote: Saying 'standing' means presence within Arafat's bounds, not a specific posture or location upon the mountain — the day is mercy, not ordeal.

title: Ihram — Entering the Sacred State
subtitle: The wardrobe, the words, and the boundaries before the House
steps: Ghusl (full wash), then perfume on the BODY before the niyyah — never on the cloths after (Bukhari 1539).
Men: two seamless white cloths, no fitted garment, no head cover. Women: ordinary modest dress; no face veil, no gloves (Bukhari 1838).
Pray two rak'ahs at the miqat, then declare: Labbaika Allahumma Hajjan (or Umrah); raise the talbiyah aloud: Labbaika Allahumma labbaik...

What ihram forbids: sewn garments (men), head cover (men), face cover and gloves (women), cutting hair or nails, perfume, hunting, marriage contracts — 'the muhrim may not marry, nor be married' (Muslim 1409).
Violations carry fidyah — fasting three days, feeding six poor persons, or sacrificing a sheep (2:196); the schools assign which expiation to which violation — ask your guide.
The talbiyah continues until the stoning of Jamrat al-Aqabah on the 10th — let your tongue not fall silent while your heart is present.
madhhabNote: Which violations require which expiation (perfume vs shaving vs intimacy) differs by school and cause — this is precisely the case for a Hajj seminar or a trusted manual.

title: How Zakat Works — The Essentials
subtitle: The third pillar: when it is due, on what, and where it goes
steps: Know the obligation: zakat joins prayer in the Qur'an again and again — 'establish prayer and give zakat' (2:43). It is not a tip on surplus feelings; it is a pillar with a name that means purification and growth (9:103).

Know the threshold (nisab): zakat is due on zakatable wealth — cash, gold, silver, trade goods, and similar — that has been held above a minimum threshold for one lunar year (hawl). The classical nisab is the value of 85 grams of gold (or 595 grams of silver — the silver standard is lower and more protective of the poor; scholars differ on which to use).

Know the rate: the standard rate on savings and trade wealth is one-fortieth — 2.5%. On certain kinds of produce and harvests, the rates are one-tenth or one-twentieth according to the type of irrigation. When in doubt, a local scholar or a reputable calculator settles the specifics of your assets.

Know the recipients: the Qur'an names them in one verse (9:60) — the poor, the needy, zakat administrators, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, the debt-ridden, in the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveler. These categories are fixed by the verse; zakat is not a general donation fund.

Give it on time: the Prophet ﷺ sent collectors and would not leave zakat of the wealthy among the people to be delayed. Delay past its year is a debt to the poor, not a savings strategy. Many Muslims give zakat al-fitr before Eid prayer as a separate, per-person obligation — ask your local scholar about it.
madhhabNote: The four schools agree on the obligation, the 2.5% rate on monetary wealth, and the hawl (lunar year). They differ on details — which nisab standard to apply, which assets count, and business-goods valuation. When your situation is complex (retirement accounts, business inventory, debts owed to you), ask a scholar who knows modern finance.

title: Giving Beyond the Obligation
subtitle: Sadaqah: the voluntary charity Allah multiplies and never wastes
steps: Understand the promise: Allah compares the giver's wealth to a grain that grows seven ears, each ear holding a hundred grains — 'and Allah multiplies for whom He wills' (2:261). The multiplication is His job description, not a metaphor under review.

Prefer the hidden coin: 'If you disclose charity, it is well; but if you conceal it and give it to the poor, it is better for you' (2:271). The left hand not knowing what the right spent is the standard — secrecy protects the gift from pride and the receiver from shame.
Know that kind speech counts: 'Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury' (2:263). A word that lifts someone is written as giving. The ledger is wider than money.

Give in the lean seasons too: the Prophet ﷺ was asked which wealth is best and answered, in meaning, the one you guard and spend in its proper avenues — even a small, steady gift outranks a large, showy one. The woman who gave a date was praised; the scale weighs sincerity with the coin.

Never fear diminishment: 'Whatever you spend of good — it is to yourselves' (2:272). Giving in this deen is transferring wealth from one of your pockets to another one Allah holds for you — one that cannot burn, depreciate, or be inherited away.
madhhabNote: Sadaqah is voluntary with no fixed rate, amount, or time — unlike zakat, which has all three. The schools agree on the general principles above; local custom governs the etiquette of giving (public collections for agreed community needs are an established exception to secrecy).

title: A Daily Portion of Qur'an
subtitle: Building a recitation practice that survives busy days
steps: Set a fixed portion, however small: the early generations were asked to keep to a daily portion (wird) and not abandon it — 'the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small' (Bukhari 6464). One page a day finishes the Qur'an in roughly eight months; half a page in a year. Small and daily beats large and abandoned.

Begin with purification: 'None touch it except the purified' (56:79). The Qur'an itself commands the state of purity for its recitation — make wudu, face the qiblah if easy, and begin with ta'awwudh (I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan — 16:98).

Recite with measured beauty: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (73:4). Slow enough to hear yourself; the tongue's hesitation over a difficult verse is written as reward. Understanding even one verse deeply is better than racing ten pages past your comprehension.

Guard the relationship from abandonment: on the Day of Judgment the Qur'an itself will complain: 'My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as a thing abandoned' (25:30). The warning is not about non-reciters alone, but about a book left on the shelf — if you have drifted, return today with one verse, not with guilt.

Bring it into the house: read aloud where children hear, even briefly. The companion who heard his father recite as a child carried it for life; hearing the Qur'an in the home is how love for it is inherited, not just taught.
madhhabNote: All schools encourage a daily wird; the juz (1/30th) system is a practical division, not a legal requirement. Listening to recitation while commuting or working is a blessed supplement — the recitation requirement itself is fulfilled by your own recitation.

title: Teaching Your Children the Deen
subtitle: Luqman's method: short sentences, daily life, and a love they can stand on
steps: Start with the foundation sentence: Luqman's first instruction to his son was tawhid — 'O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; indeed, association with Him is a great injustice' (31:13). Whatever else you teach, anchor them first to Who they are talking to.

Build the five anchors Luqman built: in a few verses he gave the whole curriculum — do not associate partners with Allah (31:13); be good to both parents even in their old age (31:14); establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you (31:17); be humble in your walk and lower your voice (31:18-19). Five sentences. A lifetime.

Use their age, not your ambition: the Prophet ﷺ taught that children be commanded to pray at seven and disciplined about it at ten (Sunan Abi Dawud 495, hasan sahih per al-Albani), and that they sleep separately at ten. Before seven, the prayer is invited, not enforced — love first, law second, and the law lands softer.

Let them catch you in the act: children believe what they see repeated, not what they hear announced. Pray where they can walk past you; say alhamdulillah out loud when the news is bad; apologize to them when you were wrong — you are teaching them repentance by being seen practicing it.

Protect the prayer from becoming a battle you always win: the goal at ten is not a child who prays from fear of you, but an adult who prays when you are not there. Win the war for their hearts even if some battles for the prayer mat are lost patiently. Allah gave Luqman wisdom; He gave you this particular child.
sources: Sunan Abi Dawud 495, hasan sahih per al-Albani
madhhabNote: The schools are united on gentleness in religious upbringing and on beginning prayer instruction young; they differ on the details of the 'at seven, at ten' narration's application. The principle every scholar affirms: mercy is the method, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young ones.'
